episodes.statement: A semantic revision bump commits the bumped node alone and leaves pinned consumers stale on purpose, so an exact backlink search finds the reconciliation work.
The impact view lists every direct and transitive dependent of a changed node in dependency order, with each edge's pinned and current revision.
The integration planner orders repairs so each pinned dependency is reconciled after its target, rereading the dependency before reconciling the consumer.
One shared verdict names a missing, mismatched, or unresolved pin for every context relation.

query.task: A shared definition changed at a higher revision. Its direct consumer updated its assumptions and bumped its own revision, so the node pinned to that consumer also mismatches. Decide the reconciliation scope and order.

gold_evidence.statement: Both pins are stale and reconciliation is consumer-owned and dependency-ordered, so the direct consumer resolves against the changed definition first and the downstream node then reconciles against it.

episodes.statement: A revision bump on a definition makes a pinned consumer stale and forces it to reread.
Cascading invalidation must identify exactly the affected consumers, including independently supported conclusions that should survive.
A consumer's conclusion can rest on a separate resolved decision that the bump did not change, so the reread confirms the conclusion while the pin is reset.
A non-behavioral internal reuse changed no consumer assumption and did not bump its owner's revision.

query.task: A consumer's pinned dependency changed at a higher revision, but the consumer's conclusion rests on a separate resolved decision that the change did not touch. Decide whether the consumer's conclusion must change.

gold_evidence.statement: The mismatch forces a reread, but the conclusion is independently supported by an unchanged decision, so it survives; the consumer resets its pin and keeps the conclusion.

episodes.statement: A committed direction was reversed after part of it had been implemented.
While the same node and scope still own the outcome, reversing it is an in-place update that bumps `context_rev` because a pinned consumer must reread the changed direction.
The reversal records the reversed commit's short identifier and subject in the node body with whether the change was kept, reverted, or replaced.
A different outcome moved to a new node and was recorded as superseded rather than reversed in place.

query.task: A downstream consumer relied on a decision whose direction was reversed inside the same owning node after partial implementation. Decide how the consumer must respond.

gold_evidence.statement: An in-place reversal bumps the owning node's revision precisely because a pinned consumer must reread and reverse its own assumption; it is not a new node and needs no supersession link.

episodes.statement: Supersede only when the outcome moves to a different node: the obsolete node is resolved, marked superseded, and records the replacement link.
Resolution does not change `context_rev`, so completion is detected from the status directory and a matching pin can still point at disposed content.
A consumer must follow the supersession link and search remaining backlinks instead of trusting a numerically matching pin.
A different outcome was reversed in place, which did bump that same node's revision.

query.task: A consumer's pinned dependency still matches the recorded revision, but the dependency now points to a replacement node and is marked disposed. Decide what the consumer must do.

gold_evidence.statement: A supersession does not change the obsolete node's revision, so a matching pin is a false negative; the consumer follows the replacement link and re-checks remaining backlinks.
